title: Unmeasured Network Connection Pooling
pattern: Creating a massive connection pool or pool size configuration for database or external API requests without measuring the live concurrency rate.
why_bad: Each connection in a pool consumes file descriptors, kernel memory buffers, and server-side thread resources. Under low traffic, a large connection pool is purely wasteful and can easily degrade network interface performance [111, 422].
detection: Initializing a database connection pool or TCP socket pool with a large default size (e.g., > 100 connections) for applications with extremely low transaction rates.
counterexample: High-volume microservices serving tens of thousands of concurrent requests per second. `Contextual`.
fix: Use a minimal default connection pool size (e.g., 5 to 10 connections) and let the pool grow dynamically only if profiled concurrency demands it.
